::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 5th 1860  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Huntington Library
:::

My dear [Sir](people/person_1143.qmd),
I have authorized [M. Tauchnitz](people/person_1396.qmd) to republish “[The Little Duke](cmy_books/cmybook_20.qmd),” and Mr [Sydney Williams](people/person_1964.qmd) tells me that he is about to apply to you for a cast of the frontispiece - I am afraid however that the lithographs can be no longer renewed, and I must reply to him that only the vignette of the little page is still to be had. I believe [Mrs Blackburn](people/person_159.qmd) had the stones broken up after the 2nd or 3rd edition.[^1]

From what I hear, I cannot but hope that <u>[Mlle Mori](other_books/otherbook_270.qmd)</u> is in a more prosperous state than when last you wrote, the [Saturday Review](organizations/other_99.qmd) was so favorable[^2] [sic], and after that and the [Guardian](organizations/other_75.qmd), the private opinions I have heard certainly became much more laudatory - I believe [Miss Roberts](people/person_1244.qmd) is just now in England, and I cannot but hope she will find her book a greater success than seemed at one time likely.

I hope by Christmas to have a [story of my own](cmy_books/cmybook_38.qmd) ready for separate publication - now coming out in the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd)

Yours faithfully
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Jemima Blackburn had provided lithographic illustrations for *The Little Duke*. The technology involved acid-burning a drawing using an oil-based medium on to limestone slabs for printing. It would seem from this and later discussions that the stones remained the property of the artist, and that Blackburn did not preserve hers for long.
[^2]: *Saturday Review* (5 May 1860) 577-8.
